local.b: The ACLU and other groups filed a class-action suit over "inhumane" treatment at Miami Correctional Facility, where many Chicago-area immigrants are held.

local.b: A new exhibit tells the story of Mary Cassatt's three-panel 1893 World's Fair mural, last known to be in Chicago in 1912.

local.b: The Lake View breakfast spot, open since 2003, will make way for Dollop Finer Diner, an outpost of Dollop Coffee Co.

local.b: Thousands of California college students have faced delays after a breach of the BankMobile app, used by about 60 community college districts to disburse aid.
local.title: Bank breach delays financial aid, forces California college students to choose between books or food

local.h: LA approves $5M for Lineage fire recovery
local.b: The City Council approved $5 million for Boyle Heights residents and businesses hit by the Lineage warehouse fire, part of a $10.5 million package.
local.title: LA approves initial $5 million to help Boyle Heights residents, businesses recover from Lineage fire

local.h: DOJ subpoenas LA County election workers
local.b: The county Registrar-Recorder confirmed grand jury subpoenas ordering election workers to appear Nov. 4.

local.h: SoCal could see first wet Halloween since 2014
local.b: Scattered showers are possible this weekend, with the highest chance Saturday night and Sunday morning and totals of half an inch to 1.5 inches.

local.h: High tides speed up Palos Verdes landslide
local.b: Land in the Portuguese Bend area is moving more than an inch a week, up from August, after storm-fueled waves eroded the coast, city officials said.

local.h: California high-speed rail CEO resigns
local.b: Ian Choudri cited personal and family priorities after a tenure troubled by budget woes, delays and the misuse of nearly $600,000 for questionable trips.

local.h: Bass and feds disagree on MacArthur Park arrests
local.b: Mayor Karen Bass said she had not approved arresting people for using drugs in the park; a federal prosecutor who oversaw the operation said she did.
local.title: Who approved arresting people for using drugs at MacArthur Park? Bass and feds disagree

local.b: Politicians, police and wildlife officers rushed to West 75th Street to stop water tower work that disturbed a nest of seven barn owls.
local.title: 'It is a crime!': Upper West Side owl lovers outraged after rooftop work wrecks nest

local.h: NYCHA says Marcy Houses asbestos removed
local.b: A steam leak left asbestos-laden residue on exterior walls in Bed-Stuy; residents had complained for weeks and some lost heat and hot water.
local.title: NYCHA says it's removed asbestos found at Brooklyn’s Marcy Houses

local.h: Suit says Two Trees illegally raised rents
local.b: A class-action lawsuit accuses the Brooklyn developer of skirting tax-break rules and illegally raising rents at one of its buildings.
local.title: Influential Brooklyn developer illegally raised rents despite tax break, lawsuit claims

local.h: Democrats' NJ-7 early vote lead keeps growing
local.b: Early turnout in New Jersey's 7th District has swamped 2024 totals, giving Democrats an edge in their bid to unseat Rep. Tom Kean Jr.
local.title: Democrats' early voting lead in NJ keeps growing ahead of Election Day

local.h: Council takes up Mamdani's community safety agency
local.b: The City Council holds a hearing Friday on creating a Department of Community Safety, one of Mayor Mamdani's top campaign promises on violence prevention and mental health response.
local.title: NYC Council takes key step toward Mamdani's promised Department of Community Safety

local.h: 8 charged in $7M SNAP fraud scheme
local.b: The Manhattan DA says the group used deli names to steal EBT card numbers from April 2023 to September 2025.
local.title: 8 people charged in $7M SNAP benefit fraud scheme

local.h: Nobody is enforcing NYC's $3 bus fare for now
local.b: Enforcement is on pause after a series of confrontations involving MTA agents, and the NYPD will not step in while the security force is suspended.
local.title: NYPD won't enforce NYC's bus fare while MTA security force is suspended

local.h: Feared EES airport chaos did not materialise
local.b: A Eurocontrol report found French and German airports were worst affected by the EU's new entry-exit checks but saw only a slight rise in summer delays.
local.title: Feared summer EES chaos at French airports 'did not materialise'

local.h: Police brace for Halloween protests in France
local.b: Interior Minister Laurent Nunez warned of a 'very high risk of public disorder' on Oct. 31 and announced around 70,000 police for the Yellow Vest and student protests.

local.h: Philippe questioned in Le Havre embezzlement case
local.b: Magistrates named presidential candidate Edouard Philippe an 'assisted witness', a less serious status than formal investigation, in a case tied to his time as Le Havre mayor.

local.h: Trappes shooting suspect targeted Muslims, Africans
local.b: The 39-year-old suspect, who killed one person and wounded seven west of Paris, admitted targeting people who appeared Muslim or African, prosecutors said.

local.h: Seattle, Tacoma ask voters for bus sales taxes
local.b: Sales tax measures on Tuesday's ballot would expand bus service, including Pierce Transit routes that have shrunk over the decades.
local.title: Seattle and Tacoma want higher sales taxes to expand bus service. Will voters go for it?

local.h: GEO Group gets $1.5B deal to run Tacoma ICE center
local.b: ICE awarded the private prison company a 10-year contract for the 1,635-bed Northwest ICE Processing Center despite reports of poor conditions.

local.b: Nearly 1,400 people died by suicide in the state in 2025, the most in 25 years, according to new health department data.
